title: Flat cokernel of a universally exact sequence
statement: Let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be a universally exact sequence of modules over a commutative ring $R$ (that is, tensoring it with every $R$-module remains exact). If $M_2$ is flat over $R$, then $M_3$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Let 0→N→N′→N″→0 be any short exact sequence of R-modules. Tensoring the given universally exact sequence with each of N, N′, and N″ yields three short exact rows, and tensoring 0→N→N′→N″→0 with the flat module M₂ yields an injective middle vertical map M₂⊗N→M₂⊗N′. The resulting commutative 3×3 diagram has exact rows and an injective middle vertical arrow.

source.place: Tag 058P, proof of lemma-ui-flat-domain, diagram setup

proof.text: Let N→N′ be any injective R-linear map and complete it to a short exact sequence 0→N→N′→N″→0 with N″ its cokernel. Let x∈M₁⊗N map to zero in M₁⊗N′. By commutativity of the left square, the image of x in M₂⊗N′ (through M₁⊗N′) equals the image under M₂⊗N→M₂⊗N′ of its image in M₂⊗N, so the latter vanishes, since M₂⊗N→M₂⊗N′ is injective (step 1). Since the top row is exact, M₁⊗N→M₂⊗N is injective, so x=0. Thus M₁⊗N→M₁⊗N′ is injective for every injection N→N′, and M₁ is flat by the definition of flatness.

source.place: Tag 058P, proof of lemma-ui-flat-domain, argument that M₁ is flat

proof.text: Keep the diagram of step 1 for an injection N→N′ with cokernel N″. Let x∈M₃⊗N map to zero in M₃⊗N′. The top row is exact, so x is the image of some y∈M₂⊗N. Let y′ be the image of y in M₂⊗N′; it maps to the image of x in M₃⊗N′, which is zero, so by exactness of the middle row y′ is the image of some z′∈M₁⊗N′. The image of z′ in M₂⊗N″ equals the image of y′ there, which is zero because N→N′→N″ is zero. The bottom row is exact, so M₁⊗N″→M₂⊗N″ is injective and z′ maps to zero in M₁⊗N″. By right exactness of M₁⊗−, the left column M₁⊗N→M₁⊗N′→M₁⊗N″→0 is exact (and short exact by the flatness of M₁ from step 2), so z′ is the image of some z∈M₁⊗N. Then y minus the image of z in M₂⊗N maps to y′−y′=0 in M₂⊗N′, and injectivity of M₂⊗N→M₂⊗N′ (step 1) gives that y is the image of z. Hence x, the image of y in M₃⊗N, is the image of an element of M₁⊗N under the composite M₁⊗N→M₂⊗N→M₃⊗N, which is zero; so x=0. Thus M₃⊗N→M₃⊗N′ is injective for every injection N→N′, and M₃ is flat by the definition of flatness.
